overview.what_is: CPC (Certified Professional Coder) is a globally recognized certification offered by AAPC (American Academy of Professional Coders). It validates a professional’s expertise in medical coding using ICD-10-CM, CPT, and HCPCS Level II code sets. CPC-certified professionals are in high demand in hospitals, medical billing companies, insurance firms, and healthcare MNCs.
overview.about: A Certified Professional Coder is a trained healthcare professional responsible for translating medical diagnoses, procedures, and services into standardized medical codes. These codes are essential for insurance claims, reimbursements, compliance, and healthcare data accuracy. CPC certification proves your ability to code accurately and ethically according to US healthcare standards.

Ensure compliance with coding guidelines and regulations
Identify and correct coding errors
Support insurance claims and reimbursement processes

Reduce claim denials and improve revenue cycle efficiency

courses.title: Certified Risk Adjustment Coder (CRC) Training
courses.description: Specialized training for risk adjustment coding in healthcare organizations.

overview.what_is: CRC (Certified Risk Adjustment Coder) is an advanced certification provided by AAPC. It validates a coder's expertise in Risk Adjustment and Hierarchical Condition Category (HCC) coding. Risk adjustment is a methodology used by CMS (Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services) and commercial payers to estimate future healthcare costs based on a patient's current health status.
overview.about: A Certified Risk Adjustment Coder is responsible for reviewing medical records to accurately capture and code chronic conditions and comorbidities using ICD-10-CM. Ensuring all diagnoses are coded accurately to the highest level of specificity directly impacts a healthcare organization's RAF (Risk Adjustment Factor) score and subsequent funding.

roles_responsibilities: Review patient charts for accurate ICD-10-CM diagnosis coding
Identify and abstract chronic and acute medical conditions
Ensure clinical documentation supports the assigned codes with the MEAT criteria (Monitor, Evaluate, Assess, Treat)
Assign accurate HCC (Hierarchical Condition Category) codes
Perform retrospective, prospective, and concurrent chart reviews
Educate providers on Clinical Documentation Improvement (CDI)
Maintain compliance with CMS guidelines to prevent fraudulent billing

training_info.description: The CRC training program at Turn Worth Academy dives deep into ICD-10-CM guidelines with a heavy focus on chronic disease coding, the MEAT concept, and Medicare Advantage (Part C) risk adjustment models.

Real-time chart review and auditing practice

courses.title: Certified Coding Specialist (CCS) Training
courses.description: Hospital-based coding certification preparation with inpatient coding focus.

overview.what_is: CCS (Certified Coding Specialist) is a credential offered by AHIMA (American Health Information Management Association). It is the gold standard for hospital-based coding. CCS professionals are experts in reviewing patient records and assigning numeric codes for diagnoses and procedures. They are proficient in the ICD-10-CM, ICD-10-PCS, and CPT coding systems.
overview.about: A Certified Coding Specialist primarily works in inpatient hospital settings. They review complex medical records to determine the correct diagnosis (ICD-10-CM) and inpatient procedure codes (ICD-10-PCS). They also apply MS-DRG (Medicare Severity Diagnosis Related Groups) classifications for hospital reimbursement.

Code complex inpatient hospital records and surgeries
Ensure accurate MS-DRG and APR-DRG assignment for reimbursement
Review medical documentation for completeness and clinical accuracy
Apply CPT and HCPCS codes for hospital outpatient services
Maintain compliance with AHIMA standards and CMS regulations
Query physicians for clarification on missing or ambiguous documentation

courses.title: ED Training (Emergency Department Coding)
courses.description: Specialized emergency department coding with critical care and trauma scenarios.

overview.what_is: Emergency Department (ED) Medical Coding involves assigning correct E/M (Evaluation and Management) codes, CPT procedure codes, and ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes for patients receiving care in a hospital's emergency room. ED coding is unique because it deals with unscheduled, acute care cases ranging from minor injuries to life-threatening trauma.
overview.about: An ED Coder must be highly skilled in deciphering fast-paced, complex ED physician documentation. They are responsible for assigning the correct ED E/M levels (99281-99285), coding bedside procedures (like suturing, intubation, CPR), and applying critical care codes when a patient's life is at risk. Accurate ED coding is vital for hospital revenue cycle management.

roles_responsibilities: Assign correct ED E/M levels (99281-99285) based on MDM or specific hospital guidelines
Identify and code bedside procedures (laceration repairs, fracture care, central lines)
Code Critical Care services (99291, 99292) based on time and medical necessity
Apply correct modifiers (e.g., 25, 59, 27) for multiple procedures and E/M on the same day
Ensure diagnosis (ICD-10-CM) codes accurately reflect the acute nature of the visit
Audit ED charts for missing documentation or unbundled services

overview.what_is: Evaluation and Management (E/M) Coding focuses on assigning CPT codes for physician-patient encounters, consultations, and hospital visits. The codes (ranging from 99202 to 99499) reflect the complexity of the patient's condition and the medical decision-making (MDM) process required to treat them.
overview.about: An E/M Coder analyzes provider documentation to determine the correct level of service for patient visits. Due to the significant guideline changes introduced in 2021 and 2023, E/M coders must be highly accurate in abstracting data based on Medical Decision Making (MDM) or Total Time spent, ensuring compliance with AMA and CMS guidelines.

Ensure maximum ethical reimbursement for provider services

overview.what_is: Surgery Medical Coding involves assigning correct CPT codes for surgical procedures performed by physicians. This specialty is complex as it requires a deep understanding of human anatomy, surgical techniques, NCCI (National Correct Coding Initiative) edits, and global surgical packages.
overview.about: A Surgery Coder is responsible for translating operative reports into billable CPT codes. They must determine the primary procedure, identify any additional or secondary procedures, and apply appropriate modifiers to ensure accurate compensation and compliance with payer guidelines.

roles_responsibilities: Identify correct CPT codes for surgical procedures
Apply surgical modifiers (Modifiers 22, 50, 51, 52, 53, 58, 59, 78, 79)
Determine Global Surgical Package inclusions and exclusions
Analyze comprehensive Operative Reports
Check NCCI edits to prevent unbundling
Code across various organ systems (Integumentary, Musculoskeletal, Cardiovascular, etc.)
Coordinate with surgeons for documentation specificity

training_info.description: The Surgery Coding training program at Turn Worth Academy provides deep insights into the 10,000 to 69,999 CPT series. We focus on complex systemic surgeries, multiple procedure rules, and correct modifier usage.
training_info.eligibility: Basic Medical Coding Knowledge / Anatomy & Physiology awareness
training_info.prerequisite: Ideal for coders looking to specialize in procedural coding

exam_overview.format: Surgical case scenarios and modifier application

academy_benefits: Led by certified surgical coding experts
In-depth breakdown of the CPT surgical section
Operative report reading and abstraction techniques
NCCI edits and bundling rules workshops
Preparation for high-paying surgical coding roles
course_features: Resume building for surgery coder roles
curriculum: The Global Surgical Package & Modifiers (22 to 82)
Nervous, Eye, and Ear System Coding

courses.title: Anaesthesia Coding Training
courses.description: Anesthesia coding with time-based calculations and physical status modifiers.

overview.what_is: Anaesthesia Medical Coding involves assigning correct CPT modifiers and codes for anesthesia services provided during surgical, therapeutic, or diagnostic procedures. It differs from regular coding because it requires calculating base units, time units, and modifying units for accurate reimbursement.
overview.about: An Anaesthesia Coder is a specialized professional who reviews anesthesia records to determine the type of anesthesia used (general, regional, MAC), calculates total anesthesia time, and applies physical status modifiers (P1-P6) and qualifying circumstances to ensure proper billing and compliance.

roles_responsibilities: Identify correct CPT anesthesia codes for respective surgical procedures
Calculate total anesthesia units (Base + Time + Modifying units)
Apply physical status modifiers (P1 to P6) correctly
Identify and code for qualifying circumstances (e.g., extreme age, emergency)
Ensure documentation supports Medical Direction (concurrency modifiers like QK, QY, GC)
Audit anesthesia records for compliance and revenue leakage prevention
Coordinate with anesthesiologists for documentation clarity

training_info.description: The Anesthesia Coding training program at Turn Worth Academy is tailored to teach coders the complex unit-based billing systems used in anesthesia. The course focuses on time calculations, modifier applications, and Medicare rules specific to anesthesia.
training_info.eligibility: Basic Medical Coding Knowledge / Surgery Coding Awareness
training_info.prerequisite: Ideal for coders looking to specialize in high-demand niche coding

exam_overview.manuals: CPT, ASA Crosswalk, RVG (Relative Value Guide)

academy_benefits: Training by experienced anesthesia coding experts
Practical training on ASA Crosswalk and RVG manuals
course_features: Focus purely on Anesthesia billing rules
curriculum: Anesthesia Terminology and Types of Anesthesia
The Anesthesia Formula (Base Units + Time Units + Modifying Units)
Medical Direction & Concurrency Modifiers (AA, QK, QY, GC, QX, QZ)

courses.title: IPDRG Training
courses.description: Inpatient DRG coding and reimbursement methodology for hospital settings.

overview.what_is: IPDRG (Inpatient Diagnosis Related Groups) is a system used by hospitals and healthcare facilities to classify hospital cases into groups for Medicare and insurance reimbursement. The DRG system uses patient diagnoses, procedures, age, sex, and discharge status to determine the appropriate payment for inpatient stays.
overview.about: An IPDRG Medical Coder is a specialized professional who assigns ICD-10-CM and ICD-10-PCS codes to inpatient records to determine the correct DRG assignment. Their role is critical in ensuring hospitals receive fair reimbursement for the complex care provided to admitted patients while maintaining strict compliance with CMS rules.

roles_responsibilities: Analyze complex inpatient medical records
Assign accurate ICD-10-CM diagnosis and ICD-10-PCS procedure codes
Identify Principal Diagnosis, Secondary Diagnoses, and Procedures
Identify MCC (Major Complication/Comorbidity) and CC (Complication/Comorbidity)
Determine correct DRG grouping for maximum ethical reimbursement
Ensure clinical documentation supports the assigned DRG
Query physicians for vague or missing clinical documentation

training_info.description: The IPDRG training program at Turn Worth Academy focuses on the complexities of inpatient hospital reimbursement. The training covers DRG methodology, MCC/CC capture, MS-DRG logic, and detailed inpatient case studies to make you a proficient hospital coder.
training_info.eligibility: Basic Medical Coding Knowledge / Anatomy & Physiology awareness
training_info.prerequisite: Ideal for coders transitioning into inpatient hospital billing

exam_overview.format: Inpatient case scenarios and grouping software logic

academy_benefits: Expert training by inpatient hospital coding specialists
Deep dive into MS-DRG and APR-DRG methodologies
Interview preparation for hospital coding roles
curriculum: Understanding the DRG (Diagnosis Related Group) System
Principal Diagnosis vs. Admitting Diagnosis Rules

courses.title: HCC Medical Coding Training
courses.description: Hierarchical Condition Category coding for risk adjustment and Medicare Advantage.

overview.what_is: HCC (Hierarchical Condition Category) Medical Coding is a risk adjustment model used to estimate future healthcare costs for patients. Introduced by CMS (Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services), HCC coding relies heavily on ICD-10-CM coding to capture chronic conditions and accurate patient risk profiles. It is primarily used in Medicare Advantage plans.
overview.about: An HCC Medical Coder specializes in reviewing patient medical records to identify and code chronic illnesses and severe conditions. Their accurate coding ensures healthcare organizations receive appropriate funding based on the complexity of patient care required. HCC coders play a crucial role in predicting patient care needs and improving healthcare quality.

roles_responsibilities: Assign accurate ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes for chronic and acute conditions
Review patient charts to capture unreported chronic illnesses
Ensure clinical documentation meets MEAT (Monitor, Evaluate, Assess, Treat) criteria
Validate undocumented or improperly coded HCC diagnoses
Educate physicians on specific clinical documentation guidelines
Support risk adjustment audits and compliance reviews
Ensure maximum alignment of disease burden and reimbursement

training_info.description: The HCC Medical Coding training program at Turn Worth Academy is designed to equip coders with risk adjustment methodologies. The course covers deep ICD-10-CM guidelines, MEAT criteria, chronic disease pathology, and RAF (Risk Adjustment Factor) scoring.
training_info.eligibility: Basic Medical Coding Knowledge / Anatomy & Physiology awareness
training_info.prerequisite: Suitable for medical coders wanting to enter risk adjustment

academy_benefits: Training by certified Risk Adjustment Coding experts
In-depth focus exclusively on ICD-10-CM & HCC guidelines
Practical training with real-time patient charts
Updated course curriculum mapping to latest CMS guidelines
Targeted placement assistance in Risk Adjustment programs
course_features: Interview prep for HCC specific roles
curriculum: Deep Dive into ICD-10-CM Guidelines for HCC
The MEAT Concept (Monitor, Evaluate, Assess, Treat)
Coding Chronic Conditions (Diabetes, Hypertension, CKD, etc.)

Practical Case Studies in Risk Adjustment
